subject: POC: StellarPay - request header for priority routing & runtime mis-ordering during bursts
messages:
From: Daniel Park <daniel.park@stellarpay.com>
To: aisha_rahman@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 5 Sep 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: intermittent latency spikes and out-of-order tokens during our POC

Hey Aisha —

Quick heads-up from our end while testing the dedicated pool yesterday. During a couple of parallel payment-validation flows we saw latency spikes (p95 jumped from ~120ms to ~450ms) and one run produced tokens that looked slightly out of order when we stream into our aggregator. The attached logs show the session ids and a short tcp dump around the window.

We suspect it’s related to concurrency from our side (multiple parallel requests from the same client process) and whatever prioritization/redelivery is happening in the runtime. Can you loop in your runtime folks? This is blocking our final SLA discussion — we need predictable streaming ordering and a way to signal high-priority requests from our orchestration layer.

Thanks,
Daniel Park
Senior Platform Engineer, StellarPay

From: aisha_rahman@redwood.com
To: dev_patel@redwood.com, logan_wright@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 6 Sep 2028 08:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: intermittent latency spikes and out-of-order tokens during our POC

Forwarding StellarPay's report — they're seeing p95 spikes and occasional streaming token re-ordering when they fire many concurrent validation calls. They asked for a way to mark a subset of requests as high-priority so they always get routed onto lower-latency queues in Dedicated.

Notes from my quick look:
- Logs show repeated connection reuse from a single client (same connection id) with bursts of 8-12 concurrent requests.
- The streaming reorder appears correlated with a retry/backpressure loop where a mid-pipeline server reacted to a resource transient.

Ask: can runtime parse a custom header (e.g., X-Client-Priority: urgent|normal) and map it to the existing request routing priority immediately for Dedicated customers (config flip) while we evaluate a more robust client-side token ordering fix? Also: can we confirm if there are TLS rehandshake events in the pcap that might explain connection stalls?

Marissa — FYI for the SLA conversation. Logan — this is a small product ask + potential runtime hotfix; need your prioritization advice.

Thanks,
Aisha
Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: dev_patel@redwood.com
To: aisha_rahman@redwood.com, logan_wright@redwood.com
Cc: tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 6 Sep 2028 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: intermittent latency spikes and out-of-order tokens during our POC

Thanks for the details + logs. Quick triage notes after a local run of the pcap and logs:

- I see bursts causing queue oversubscription on one worker host; when oversubscribed the runtime will batch and occasionally reorder stream fragments when a fallback worker picks up the remaining KV cache updates. That matches the token ordering symptom.
- No TLS renegotiation events in the pcap, but there are a few sub-second TCP retransmits during the spike window — looks like transient packet loss in the customer's path.

Feasible short-term mitigations (fastest-to-deliver):
1) Config flip: honor X-Client-Priority header at the edge and route to an isolated priority queue for Dedicated pools (config change + small router rule). Estimated ~1 business day to implement and can be canaried for a single customer.
2) Temporary runtime guard: detect high fanout from a single connection and cap concurrency per-conn to N=6 with “429-suggest-retry” and include a structured retry-after token. This is slightly risky for their throughput but will stabilize ordering. ~1 day to implement.

Longer-term fixes: header-based priority should be formalized (SDK/Docs + signed header semantics) and we should add stronger KV-cache handoff invariants to avoid reordering when tasks are migrated mid-response. That's a small engineering project (2-3 sprints) to fully eliminate edge-case reorder.

I can deliver the config flip + guard into canary tomorrow if leadership signs off. Need: (a) product approval to expose X-Client-Priority semantics (even if proprietary to Dedicated), (b) SRE to schedule a single-customer canary window, (c) legal/procurement flagging if we change SLA behavior.

-- Dev Patel
Senior Runtime Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: logan_wright@redwood.com
To: dev_patel@redwood.com, aisha_rahman@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 7 Sep 2028 07:55:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: intermittent latency spikes and out-of-order tokens during our POC

Agree with the canary plan. A few product notes and constraints:

- We can support an opt-in header for Dedicated customers but it must be gated: documented, included in the Dedicated TOS addendum, and limited to routing hints only (no guarantees beyond routing preference). We should avoid promising strict ordering at the API level until we implement the KV-cache invariant fix.
- Ask SRE to run the canary during off-peak US morning (we'll coordinate with StellarPay). Aisha/Marissa — capture the exact SLA language we will propose if the interim fix is accepted (we should avoid open-ended credits).
- Dev: implement the header flip as a runtime config (feature flag) scoped to tenant id; include telemetry that logs header presence, queue chosen, and any 429s emitted. We need that telemetry to evaluate impact before any contractual commitment.

I'll own the product-side comms and the TOS addendum language. Tessa — can you schedule the SRE slot and draft the rollback plan for the canary? Marissa — I need you to align StellarPay on acceptance criteria we can measure during the canary (p95 < 180ms, no reordering events across 2 hours of burst test).

Thanks,
Logan Wright
Product Manager, Redwood Inference
From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Daniel Park <daniel.park@stellarpay.com>, aisha_rahman@redwood.com
Cc: logan_wright@redwood.com, dev_patel@redwood.com, tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 7 Sep 2028 16:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC: StellarPay - request header for priority routing & runtime mis-ordering during bursts

Daniel — thanks for the quick escalation and for the traces. We have a concrete plan:

1) Tomorrow morning (09/08) we’ll enable a tenant-scoped feature flag that honors a new header X-Client-Priority for your Dedicated pool. The runtime will attempt to route requests with value “urgent” into an isolated priority queue.
2) If we detect >8 concurrent inflight requests from the same connection during the canary, the runtime will return 429-suggest-retry with a Retry-After header instead of letting the queue oversubscribe. That is reversible and will be monitored.
3) Acceptance criteria: during the 2-hour burst test window we’ll measure p95 and token-ordering; if p95 <= 180ms and no reordering incidents are seen, we’ll consider this resolved for the POC and document the header behavior in a short addendum.

We’ll send a small signed addendum that documents the routing hint semantics (no absolute ordering guarantee) and a one-time SLA credit if we miss the canary acceptance thresholds due to runtime faults.

Can you confirm the 09/08 10:00–12:00 PDT test window works for you? If yes, I’ll lock in SRE and provide the addendum draft to procurement.

— Marissa Cole
Sales Engineering, Redwood Inference
